bull.b: Rapid growth in HPC leasing is shifting TeraWulf toward contracted infrastructure revenue, potentially making the business less dependent on bitcoin mining economics. Continued conversion of operating capacity into leases could support more predictable revenue and stronger long-term utilization.

A large, long-duration lease provides substantial revenue visibility if delivery and financing milestones are achieved. Google credit support further strengthens the contractual framework, helping TeraWulf translate scarce power and data-center capacity into durable infrastructure cash flows.

Significant liquidity and expanded revolving capacity give TeraWulf more flexibility to fund contracted projects, letters of credit, and remaining commitments without immediately relying on equity issuance. This supports execution continuity while management seeks to limit dilution.

bear.b: Revenue growth and gross margin have not yet translated into sustainable earnings because operating and other expenses overwhelm gross profit. Persistent losses can reduce internal funding capacity, increase reliance on external capital, and weaken resilience if project execution takes longer.

bear.t: Heavy Capital Requirements And Cash Burn
bear.b: Deeply negative free cash flow combined with substantial remaining project spending creates a continuing need for financing and disciplined capital allocation. Large commitments may limit flexibility elsewhere and increase the consequences of cost overruns, delays, or weaker-than-expected project cash generation.

Muskie's expansion potential is not fully supported by signed customer contracts, so future capacity may take longer to monetize than planned. Delayed contracting could leave capital tied up without corresponding lease revenue and make the broader growth plan more dependent on execution and customer selection.
